qualification: The initial private two-session hinge gain of about 8% does not reproduce after exact-SHA rebuild/copy. Identical-code placement tests retain differences around 8-9% even with normalized argv0; cause not identified. Earlier capture-time scopes mentioning hinge gains are superseded here. Scoped functional proofs, source/binary bindings and numerical checks are unchanged.
interpretation: Retain the scoped Scale_Row optimization for the consistently improved chain24 workload. Latest randomized-copy medians reduce chain time about 1.9-2.1%, with replica/block bootstrap intervals below one in all three states; normal C remains about 2.3 times faster there. Other model effects are placement-sensitive/inconclusive, and the small hinge regression in the first replica session is not excluded. No arbitrary noise threshold, unweighted cross-model mean or claim of all-workload improvement/parity.
limitations: Three replicas per implementation and bootstrap intervals describe these sampled placements, not a universal distribution or portable speedup.
The normal pinned C shared library is the same unchanged object for all three copied C launchers; its file placement is not independently varied.
Smooth Euler supported models only; full MuJoCo features/Gold/physical accuracy and C parity remain unfinished.
